findings.title: AttributeError when accessing organization_context.member for non-members (e.g. superusers)
findings.body: `organization_context.member` can be `None` when the request is made by a user who is not a member of the organization (or if short-circuit evaluation falls through when `request.user.is_superuser` is False and `organization_context.member` is `None`). Accessing `organization_context.member.has_global_access` without checking if `organization_context.member` is `None` can raise `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'`.

findings.title: `self.paginate()` does not accept `enable_advanced_features` and `OptimizedCursorPaginator` breaks on `datetime` fields
findings.body:
In `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get`, `self.paginate(...)` is called with `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator`, `order_by='-datetime'`, and `enable_advanced_features=True`. This will fail for two reasons:
1. `Endpoint.paginate` only forwards specific arguments to `paginator_cls` (`max_limit`, `on_results`, `paginator_kwargs`, etc.) unless passed via `paginator_kwargs={'enable_advanced_features': True}`; passing `enable_advanced_features` directly to `self.paginate` raises a `TypeError: paginate() got an unexpected keyword argument 'enable_advanced_features'`.
2. `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` directly on `getattr(item, 'datetime')` (which is a `datetime.datetime` instance on `AuditLogEntry`) and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric `cursor.value` instead of converting a timestamp back to a `datetime` object like `DateTimePaginator` does. This causes a `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` when building cursors and invalid SQL comparisons when querying.

findings.title: Django `QuerySet` does not support negative slicing offsets, causing `ValueError`
findings.body: Both `BasePaginator.get_result` (when `cursor.is_prev` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`) and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 877-886) pass a negative `start_offset` (and potentially negative `stop`) into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Contrary to the comments, Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly forbids negative indexing/slicing (`if (k.start is not None and k.start < 0) or (k.stop is not None and k.stop < 0): raise ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.')`). Any request supplying a cursor with a negative offset (e.g. `cursor=0:-1:1` on any `BasePaginator` endpoint, or `cursor=0:-1:0` with `OptimizedCursorPaginator`) will crash with an unhandled `ValueError` (HTTP 500) instead of clamping to 0 or raising `BadPaginationError`.
